'''Arden Warner''' (born 1965 or 1964<ref name="NNews_BB_WarnerGenArt" />) is a Barbadian-American particle [[physicist]] and [[inventor]], working at the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] (Fermilab), notable for the creation of a novel environmentally positive, magnetism-based method for cleaning up [[oil spill]]s, now being developed by Fermilab and a company led by Warner.

==Early life and education==
Arden Ayube Warner<ref name="CCNY_CUNY_2004-5_Warner">{{cite book |title=City College of New York – Annual Report 2004-2005 |date=2005 |publisher=City College, City University of New York |location=New York City |page=8 |url=https://www.ccny.cuny.edu/sites/default/files/engineering/upload/Grove-Annual-Report-2004-2005.pdf}}</ref> was born in Barbados, in Eagle Hall, a part of the capital, [[Bridgetown]], in [[Saint Michael, Barbados|St Michael]] parish. He had a number of brothers and sisters.<ref name="RWarner_Obit_ref_brother">{{cite web |title=Roosevelt Warner |url=https://lyndhurstfuneralhome.com/events/roosevelt-warner/ |website=Lyndhurst Funeral Home |access-date=August 16, 2021 |date=April 29, 2021 |quote=Brother of Ean Warner, Keith Hinds (UK) / Philmore and Rawle Warner, Vanthyia Blackman, Dr Arden Warner, Sonia Warner-Gaskin, Shanell Warner-Brathwaite (all of the USA) / and the late MacHenley Warner, Wendell Warner, Tyronne Catlyn, Carlisle Catlyn. ... Brother-in-law of Rossana Warner, Vernice and Yvette Cummins, Junie Cummins (of Canada), Deborah and Eulalie Warner, Mitch Blackman, Dr Lena Hatchett, Leroy Gaskin, Leon Brathwaite (all of the USA)}}</ref> He attended school at Wesley Hall Boys’ School, King Street, and [[Combermere School]], Waterford, Bridgetown.<ref name="NNews_BB_WarnerGenArt">{{cite news |last1=Carter |first1=Gercine |title=Bajan's wand ready for next oil spill |url=https://www.nationnews.com/2017/04/09/bajans-wand-ready-for-next-oil-spill/ |access-date=August 15, 2021 |work=NationNews.com |date=April 9, 2017 |location=St Michael, Barbados}}</ref> He was brought up by his mother, a shopkeeper, and after he completed school, they moved to the USA, where he secured a scholarship to City College of New York, within [[City University of New York]], and later graduated with a degree in engineering and physics from [[Columbia University]].<ref name="NNews_BB_WarnerGenArt"/>

Having worked with some of the US's national laboratories, Warner interned at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] (SLAC), and won a fellowship to support his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] studies.<ref name="NNews_BB_WarnerGenArt"/>

==Career==
===Particle physics===
Warner secured employment in the Accelerator Division of the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (often known as ''Fermilab''), [[Batavia, Illinois|Batavia]], just outside [[Chicago]], Illinois,<ref name="FermiLab_Warner">{{cite news |last1=Armitage |first1=Hanae |title=Accelerator physicist invents new way to clean up oil spills |url=https://www.fnal.gov/pub/today/archive/archive_2014/today14-07-30.html |access-date=August 15, 2021 |work=Fermilab Today |publisher=Fermi National Accelarator Laboratory |date=July 30, 2014}}</ref><ref name="NNews_BB_WarnerGenArt"/> where he had been working 26 years by early 2021.<ref name="Fermilab_210222">{{cite web |last1=Barbu |first1=Brianna |title=One minute with Arden Warner, accelerator physicist |url=https://news.fnal.gov/2021/02/one-minute-with-arden-warner-accelerator-physicist/ |website=Fermilab |access-date=August 15, 2021 |location=Batavia, IL |date=February 22, 2021}}</ref>  He currently works on the Proton Improvement Plan II, one of Fermilab's major projects.<ref name="PIP_II_memship">{{cite web |title=Proton Improvement Plan II |url=https://pip2.fnal.gov/people/team-members/ |website=PIP2 at Fermilab |publisher=Fermilab |access-date=August 15, 2021}}</ref>

Warner also works as a mentor for internees,<ref name="Sample_intern-mentee_19">{{cite web |title=STEM Inspiration leads Argonne Intern on Electrical Engineering Path |url=https://www.energy.gov/articles/stem-inspiration-leads-argonne-intern-electrical-engineering-path |website=Department of Energy (US) |access-date=August 18, 2021 |date=March 26, 2019}}</ref> and has been a member of the steering body at times since the early 1980s of Fermilab's inclusive Summer Internships in Science and Technology (SIST) program, the longest-running of the Department of Energy National Laboratory system's internship programs.<ref name="SIST_at_Fermilab">{{cite web |title=Summer Internships in Science & Technology (SIST) |url=https://diversity.fnal.gov/sist/ |website=Fermilab |access-date=August 18, 2021 |quote=... the longest operating internship program in the Department of Energy National Laboratory system ...}}</ref> As of 2021, he chairs this program.<ref name="Fermilab_210222"/>

===Oil spill cleanup technology===
The US [[Department of Energy]] sought input from the scientists of the national laboratories as it struggled to deal with the cleanup required after the [[Deepwater Horizon]] event. With his wife's encouragement, Warner devised and tested an approach involving [[magnetite]] and booms which, with Fermilab support, he patented.<ref name="NNews_BB_WarnerGenArt"/> The technique has been described as especially environmentally friendly, as magnetite is naturally occurring,<ref name="GrOpt_Magnetite">{{cite web |title=Cleaning Oil Spills with Abundant Earth Magnet |url=https://www.greenoptimistic.com/oil-spills-cleaning-magnetite/ |website=Green Optimistic |access-date=August 18, 2021 |date=January 21, 2016}}</ref> and can be largely captured and reused.<ref name="FermiLab_Warner" /> It has been mentioned in a range of magazines, including ''[[Scientific American]]''<ref name="SciAm_2014">{{cite magazine |last1=Biello |first1=David |magazine=[[Scientific American]] |title=Spill Some Oil? Magnetize It for Cleanup |date=August 7, 2014 |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/podcast/episode/spill-some-oil-magnetize-it-for-cleanup/ |access-date=August 20, 2021}}</ref> and ''[[Popular Science]]''.<ref name="Pop_Sci_">{{cite magazine |last1=Gertz |first1=Emily |magazine=Popular Science |title=To Clean Up Oil Spills, Magnetize The Oil First |date=August 7, 2014 |url=https://www.popsci.com/article/science/clean-oil-spills-magnetize-oil-first/ |access-date=August 20, 2021}}</ref> Warner was a speaker at a [[TED (conference)|TED]]x conference in [[Naperville]], near Chicago, in 2015.<ref name="TEDxN_2015">{{cite web |title=TEDxNaperville: Theme:SHIFT |url=https://www.ted.com/tedx/events/14792 |website=TED.com |publisher=TED |access-date=August 28, 2021 |date=November 6, 2015 |quote=...Arden now has a doctorate, working by day as an Accelerator physicist at Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory and after hours as a tinkerer, attempting to solve problems...}}</ref>

As of 2019, the technology, which was elaborated as "electromagnetic boom and MOP",<ref name="E-MOP conf paper">{{cite journal |last1=Warner |first1=Arden |last2=Cathey |first2=David |last3=Cullen |first3=Gary |last4=Kasper |first4=Peter |last5=Lumpkin |first5=Alex |last6=Nelson |first6=John |title=Development of the Electromagnetic Boom and MOP System (EMOP) |journal=Proceedings of the 6th Int. Beam Instrumentation Conf. |date=2018 |volume=IBIC2017 |pages=1–5 |doi=10.18429/JACoW-IBIC2017-TULAB1 |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/1656416 |access-date=August 20, 2021}}</ref> was being scaled up for commercial use by a company licensed by Fermilab and led by Warner.<ref name="PhysOrg_Sauers_on_FermiOilSpillT">{{cite web |last1=Sauers (Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory) |first1=Aaron |title=Meet the new prototype in electromagnetic oil spill remediation technology |url=https://phys.org/news/2019-10-prototype-electromagnetic-oil-remediation-technology.html |website=phys.org |access-date=August 15, 2021 |date=October 11, 2019}}</ref>

Warner's idea was an inspiration for Irish student scientist [[Fionn Ferreira]] in his invention of a method for cleaning [[microplastics]] from the oceans.<ref name="SocforSci_fullabs_Ferreira">{{Cite web|title=An Investigation into the Removal of Microplastics from Water Using Ferrofluids (ISEF, Booth:CHEM004)|url=https://abstracts.societyforscience.org/Home/FullAbstract?ProjectId=14829|access-date=May 26, 2021|website=abstracts.societyforscience.org}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* Lead author for ''The design and implementation of the machine protection system for the Fermilab electron cooling facility'', Warner et al., Fermilab, May 2009<ref name="InspHEP_ref_Warner_ppr_0905">{{cite web |last1=Warner |first1=Arden |others=et al.|title=The design and implementation of the machine protection system for the Fermilab electron cooling facility |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/822289 |website=INSPIRE (HEP – High-Energy Physics) |access-date=August 15, 2021 |date=May 1, 2009}}</ref>
* Lead author for ''Machine Protection System Research and Development for the Fermilab PIP-II Proton Linac'', Warner et al., Fermilab, October 2017<ref name="InspHEP_ref_Warner_ppr_171008-13">{{cite web |last1=Warner |others=et al. |first1=Arden |title=Machine Protection System Research and Development for the Fermilab PIP-II Proton Linac |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/1656416 |website=INSPIRE (HEP – High-Energy Physics) |access-date=August 15, 2021 |date=October 8, 2017}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Warner was one of 50 recipients of the ''Barbados Jubilee Honour'' in 2016.<ref name="NNews_BB_WarnerGenArt"/>

==Personal life==
Warner is married.<ref name="Fermilab_210222" /> He is a member of the board of a Barbadian youth development [[Non-governmental organization|NGO]], The Millennium Fund.<ref name="Mill_Fund_BB_BoD">{{cite web |title=Meet the Board |url=https://millennium-fund.org/board.html |website=The Millennium Fund |location=Barbados}}</ref>
